subject: Order Form: invoicing cadence, split entities & VAT accruals
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@stellix.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-21T13:05:00+00:00
Subject: Draft order form and invoicing cadence

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Attaching our latest order form and the pricing schedule. Two quick asks so we can finalize with legal/finance on both sides:

1) Can you confirm whether Stellix will accept a single invoice for the entire EU entity group or if you require separate invoices per entity (we saw mixed signals from procurement)?
2) On VAT treatment: if Stellix can provide a tax residency certificate, our finance team can apply the reverse-charge where applicable and avoid gross-up on our invoices.

I’ve cc’d Marcus (sales lead) and Kimberly (billing/legal) to coordinate redlines and finalize net terms.

Proposed next steps:
- You send any redlines by EOD Thursday
- We incorporate and propose either a split-invoice cadence or a single consolidated invoice option with sample prorated schedule

Attachments: Stellix_OrderForm_v2_redline.pdf; OrderForm-pricing-schedule.xlsx

Best,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@stellix.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@stellix.com, legal@stellix.com
Date: 2026-12-21T15:40:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Draft order form and invoicing cadence

Ben / Marcus —

Thanks — have attached our annotated redline (see Stellix_OrderForm_v2_redline.pdf). Key points from procurement/legal:
- Stellix prefers separate invoices per legal entity for SAP/AP reconciliation.
- Net terms asked: Net 60 from invoice date (our standard).
- VAT: we will supply a tax residency certificate but we need Redwood to state clearly in the order form that VAT will be handled per-entity and that any gross-up is the vendor’s responsibility unless we provide contrary written evidence.

We also flagged the minimum commit language (section 2.3) — finance is asking whether the commit can be split across two entities on a pro-rata basis if we provide PO references for both.

Can Marcus / Kimberly comment on the operational impact of separate-entity invoicing and whether a Net 60 term is possible under the current commercial offer?

Best,
Olivia
Head of Procurement, Stellix
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-21T16:12:00+00:00
Subject: Fwd: Draft order form and invoicing cadence — internal

Kimberly —

Looping you in on Stellix’s redlines. Quick summary for legal/billing:
- They request separate invoices per legal entity (SAP constraint).
- Net 60 requested (we usually do Net 45 for mid-market; dedicated/enterprise deals sometimes allowed Net 60 with credit review).
- They want explicit VAT per-entity language and to avoid vendor gross-up if they provide residency proof.
- They asked whether minimum commit (2.3) can be split pro-rata across two entities and tied to two POs.

Questions:
1) Is separate-entity invoicing feasible from Redwood’s side without introducing duplicate billing entities for revenue recognition? What’s the simplest approach operationally?
2) Legal: What language tweak would protect Redwood from VAT gross-up exposure while accommodating residency certificates?
3) Credit/Finance: Do we allow Net 60 for this account given size and existing relationship? Ben — do you have ARR / credit history details?

Can you propose a short clause we can send back to Olivia that balances Stellix’s operational needs with our revenue recognition and collections controls?

Thanks —
Marcus
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-21T18:03:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Draft order form and invoicing cadence — internal

Marcus / Ben —

Quick take after reviewing:
- Separate invoices per legal entity: operationally fine. We will invoice by remit-to entity and include a single consolidated statement option if Stellix requests it, but revenue will be recognized against the legal entity that signs the order. We need PO numbers for each invoice to ensure match to payments.
- VAT/gross-up: propose this language for the Order Form (one-liner to insert under Tax section): "If Customer provides valid tax residency or VAT registration documentation to Vendor prior to issuance of the relevant invoice, Vendor will apply VAT treatment consistent with such documentation and Customer will not be entitled to require Vendor to gross-up amounts for VAT except where expressly agreed in writing."
- Net terms: Net 60 is acceptable subject to credit approval. Recommend we draft: "Payment terms: Net 60 days from invoice date for Customer entity(ies) listed in the applicable Purchase Order, subject to credit approval. Vendor reserves the right to invoice in advance of the start of a billing period where prepayment is required."
- Minimum commit split: we can allow pro-rata allocation if both entities are named in the Order Form and PO numbers are provided. Need a short handling paragraph: "Minimum Commit Allocation: Customer may allocate the Minimum Commit across multiple Customer entities by specifying allocation percentages and corresponding Purchase Order numbers at time of execution; Vendor will invoice allocated amounts to each specified entity."

I’ve drafted redline snippets — will attach a short exhibit and can push to Ben to share with Stellix. Recommend we accept separate-invoice path with the above protective language.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Revenue & Contracts
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@stellix.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@stellix.com
Date: 2026-12-22T10:18:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Draft order form and invoicing cadence

Olivia —

Thanks for the detailed redline. Per internal review (cc’d Kimberly and Marcus):
- We can issue separate invoices per legal entity. Please include the PO number and remit-to entity for each invoice line in your signature block or return the attached allocation table.
- Kimberly has proposed tax language (see below) that we’ll insert under the Tax section; if Stellix can provide the TaxResidency_Certificate.pdf we will apply reverse-charge where appropriate and not gross-up amounts.
- Net 60: we’re happy to accept Net 60 pending standard credit approval. I’ll initiate a quick credit check — if any concerns arise we’ll flag before execution.
- Minimum commit: we can accept a pro-rata split; please confirm allocation percentages and attach the two PO references.

Next steps:
1) Please send the completed allocation table and PO numbers (simple two-line CSV or the attached Excel)
2) Provide the tax residency certificate on company letterhead
3) We’ll update the redline and send final for signature via DocuSign (link to follow)

Attachments referenced: OrderForm-pricing-schedule.xlsx; Stellix_TaxResidency_Certificate.pdf (Stellix to provide)

Best,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
